captures.title: Configuration
captures.text:
System
›
Configuration
Configuration
Save
Durations
Every request is time-bound unless the requester chooses standing access and gives a second reason. Expiry revokes through the same path as provisioning. Set by the product, not edited here.
Offered
8 hours, 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, Standing
Standing
Needs its own reason of at least 20 characters
Stewards
Who approves after the manager, resolved from the directory at decision time. Set by the product, not edited here.
Work roles
Holders of hr-admin in Work
Assessment roles
Holders of program-lead in Assessment
Social roles
Holders of community-admin in Social
Pipelines roles
Holders of pipeline-admin in Pipelines
Initiatives
The initiative’s owner
Work capabilities
The budget owner: holders of org-leader in Work
Sensitive items
An access admin, as a final step
Escalation and delegation
A step nobody decides in time reaches the next tier of deciders; its own deciders keep the right. Approvers hand their decisions on while away under Settings. The wait is set when the service is deployed.
Time limit
48 hours per step, counted from when it starts waiting
Then
The access admins, then after another 48 hours the platform admins (an access-admin step goes straight to the platform admins)
Delegation
Up to 30 days, to another approver; never on their own requests, and an access-admin step only to an access admin
Catalog items
Each item’s default duration and whether it is sensitive (adds an access-admin step). Saved changes apply to requests submitted afterwards.

On this page
Full width
You are triaging one piece of evidence about a software engineering team, before it is scored against a maturity rubric.
Input
Parse these from $ARGUMENTS (labeled, space-separated, any order; values may be quoted):
document: — required. Repo-root-relative path to the document, e.g. workspace/teams/<team-id>/raw_transcripts/interview.vtt.
If document: is missing, STOP and say so. Do not guess.
Read the document at the document: path.
Supported transcript/document inputs in this flow are the text formats .vtt, .md, and .txt. Binary formats (.pdf, .docx, .xlsx, images) cannot be read directly — they are converted to a sibling <original-filename>.md during ingestion. If the document: path points at a binary file, read that sibling .md instead; if it does not exist, STOP and report that the file has not been ingested yet. Never infer a classification from a filename.
Also read the rubric dimension list from sdlcd/assessment/dimensions/rubric.yaml to get the dimension IDs and titles.
Task
Given the document's type and length, judge:
evidence_type: one of stakeholder_interview, assessment_qa, document, survey, meeting, other
weight: high, medium, or low — how much this evidence should move the team's score. A short survey answer or brief meeting note carries less weight than a full stakeholder interview.
weight_reason: one short sentence explaining the weight (mention type and/or length)
informs: brief human-readable list of maturity areas this evidence touches (e.g. "testing", "deployment", "incident response")
relevant_dimension_ids: from the rubric dimensions, the IDs of ONLY the dimensions this evidence gives real, direct signal about — enough to assess or update that dimension's level. Omit dimensions the evidence does not substantively address. Being precise here protects scores on dimensions this evidence is silent about.
action_items: short clarifying commitments/to-dos mentioned, if any (empty array if none)
summary: 1-2 sentences summarizing the evidence
Output
Write your classification as JSON to the team's temp directory. For example, for a team whose id is <team-id>:
Copy
workspace/teams/<team-id>/temp/classification.json
Use this exact schema:
Copy
{
 "evidence_type": "stakeholder_interview",
 "weight": "high",
 "weight_reason": "Detailed 45-minute stakeholder interview covering multiple practices.",
 "informs": ["testing", "CI/CD", "incident response"],
 "relevant_dimension_ids": ["1", "5", "12"],
 "action_items": [],
 "summary": "The team discussed their testing and deployment practices in depth.",
 "length_chars": 12345
}
Then run this command to validate and persist the classification:
Copy
uv run -m sdlcd.main assess apply-classification workspace/teams/<TEAM-ID>/temp/classification.json --team <TEAM-ID>
<TEAM-ID> is the team segment of the document: path (the <team-id> in workspace/teams/<team-id>/...). If the path has no team segment, STOP and report that — do not guess a team.
Writing the file is not the end of the job. relevant_dimension_ids decides which dimensions a later /score-dimensions pass touches at all, so it is validated strictly by this verb: ids must be plain rubric dimension numbers ("1".."17", never "DIM-01"), with no duplicates, and evidence_type/weight must match the vocabulary above. If the verb exits non-zero, fix the JSON and run it again — do not report success on an unapplied classification.
Report: the evidence type, weight and weight reason, the relevant dimension ids, and the path the verb printed.

On this page
Full width
You are triaging one piece of evidence about a software engineering team, before it is scored against a maturity rubric.
Input
Parse these from $ARGUMENTS (labeled, space-separated, any order; values may be quoted):
document: — required. Repo-root-relative path to the document, e.g. workspace/teams/<team-id>/raw_transcripts/interview.vtt.
If document: is missing, STOP and say so. Do not guess.
Read the document at the document: path.
Supported transcript/document inputs in this flow are the text formats .vtt, .md, and .txt. Binary formats (.pdf, .docx, .xlsx, images) cannot be read directly — they are converted to a sibling <original-filename>.md during ingestion. If the document: path points at a binary file, read that sibling .md instead; if it does not exist, STOP and report that the file has not been ingested yet. Never infer a classification from a filename.
Also read the rubric dimension list from sdlcd/assessment/dimensions/rubric.yaml to get the dimension IDs and titles.
Task
Given the document's type and length, judge:
evidence_type: one of stakeholder_interview, assessment_qa, document, survey, meeting, other
weight: high, medium, or low — how much this evidence should move the team's score. A short survey answer or brief meeting note carries less weight than a full stakeholder interview.
weight_reason: one short sentence explaining the weight (mention type and/or length)
informs: brief human-readable list of maturity areas this evidence touches (e.g. "testing", "deployment", "incident response")
relevant_dimension_ids: from the rubric dimensions, the IDs of ONLY the dimensions this evidence gives real, direct signal about — enough to assess or update that dimension's level. Omit dimensions the evidence does not substantively address. Being precise here protects scores on dimensions this evidence is silent about.
action_items: short clarifying commitments/to-dos mentioned, if any (empty array if none)
summary: 1-2 sentences summarizing the evidence
Output
Write your classification as JSON to the team's temp directory. For example, for a team whose id is <team-id>:
Copy
workspace/teams/<team-id>/temp/classification.json
Use this exact schema:
Copy
{
 "evidence_type": "stakeholder_interview",
 "weight": "high",
 "weight_reason": "Detailed 45-minute stakeholder interview covering multiple practices.",
 "informs": ["testing", "CI/CD", "incident response"],
 "relevant_dimension_ids": ["1", "5", "12"],
 "action_items": [],
 "summary": "The team discussed their testing and deployment practices in depth.",
 "length_chars": 12345
}
Then run this command to validate and persist the classification:
Copy
uv run -m sdlcd.main assess apply-classification workspace/teams/<TEAM-ID>/temp/classification.json --team <TEAM-ID>
<TEAM-ID> is the team segment of the document: path (the <team-id> in workspace/teams/<team-id>/...). If the path has no team segment, STOP and report that — do not guess a team.
Writing the file is not the end of the job. relevant_dimension_ids decides which dimensions a later /score-dimensions pass touches at all, so it is validated strictly by this verb: ids must be plain rubric dimension numbers ("1".."17", never "DIM-01"), with no duplicates, and evidence_type/weight must match the vocabulary above. If the verb exits non-zero, fix the JSON and run it again — do not report success on an unapplied classification.
Report: the evidence type, weight and weight reason, the relevant dimension ids, and the path the verb printed.

On this page
Full width
You are triaging one piece of evidence about a software engineering team, before it is scored against a maturity rubric.
Input
Parse these from $ARGUMENTS (labeled, space-separated, any order; values may be quoted):
document: — required. Repo-root-relative path to the document, e.g. workspace/teams/<team-id>/raw_transcripts/interview.vtt.
If document: is missing, STOP and say so. Do not guess.
Read the document at the document: path.
Supported transcript/document inputs in this flow are the text formats .vtt, .md, and .txt. Binary formats (.pdf, .docx, .xlsx, images) cannot be read directly — they are converted to a sibling <original-filename>.md during ingestion. If the document: path points at a binary file, read that sibling .md instead; if it does not exist, STOP and report that the file has not been ingested yet. Never infer a classification from a filename.
Also read the rubric dimension list from sdlcd/assessment/dimensions/rubric.yaml to get the dimension IDs and titles.
Task
Given the document's type and length, judge:
evidence_type: one of stakeholder_interview, assessment_qa, document, survey, meeting, other
weight: high, medium, or low — how much this evidence should move the team's score. A short survey answer or brief meeting note carries less weight than a full stakeholder interview.
weight_reason: one short sentence explaining the weight (mention type and/or length)
informs: brief human-readable list of maturity areas this evidence touches (e.g. "testing", "deployment", "incident response")
relevant_dimension_ids: from the rubric dimensions, the IDs of ONLY the dimensions this evidence gives real, direct signal about — enough to assess or update that dimension's level. Omit dimensions the evidence does not substantively address. Being precise here protects scores on dimensions this evidence is silent about.
action_items: short clarifying commitments/to-dos mentioned, if any (empty array if none)
summary: 1-2 sentences summarizing the evidence
Output
Write your classification as JSON to the team's temp directory. For example, for a team whose id is <team-id>:
Copy
workspace/teams/<team-id>/temp/classification.json
Use this exact schema:
Copy
{
 "evidence_type": "stakeholder_interview",
 "weight": "high",
 "weight_reason": "Detailed 45-minute stakeholder interview covering multiple practices.",
 "informs": ["testing", "CI/CD", "incident response"],
 "relevant_dimension_ids": ["1", "5", "12"],
 "action_items": [],
 "summary": "The team discussed their testing and deployment practices in depth.",
 "length_chars": 12345
}
Then run this command to validate and persist the classification:
Copy
uv run -m sdlcd.main assess apply-classification workspace/teams/<TEAM-ID>/temp/classification.json --team <TEAM-ID>
<TEAM-ID> is the team segment of the document: path (the <team-id> in workspace/teams/<team-id>/...). If the path has no team segment, STOP and report that — do not guess a team.
Writing the file is not the end of the job. relevant_dimension_ids decides which dimensions a later /score-dimensions pass touches at all, so it is validated strictly by this verb: ids must be plain rubric dimension numbers ("1".."17", never "DIM-01"), with no duplicates, and evidence_type/weight must match the vocabulary above. If the verb exits non-zero, fix the JSON and run it again — do not report success on an unapplied classification.
Report: the evidence type, weight and weight reason, the relevant dimension ids, and the path the verb printed.
